esp32_part: I2S MEMS mic, such as INMP441
calculation: Scenario dose % = 100 x 2^((TWA8 - 85) / 3) x hours / 9; published TWA8 values are already 8-hour normalised, so no 9/8 factor
limits: 85 dBA and 3 dB exchange are NIOSH; 30 days is a placeholder; the mic needs testing against a Type 2 meter

calculation: SED per hour = UV index x 0.9; dataset values are horizontal ambient model doses, NOT personal doses
trigger: 30 days with peak UV index of 8 or more, and 5+ years outdoors
limits: WHO, ICNIRP constants confirmed; 30 J/m2 ICNIRP limit is about 1.0-1.3 SED of sunlight; salt reflection only measured at Salar de Uyuni (Reuder 2007); low-cost UV sensors need per-unit calibration (Serrano 2022)

calculation: Colour match to a urine chart validated in non-workers
trigger: Score of 5 or more on a hot day, twice in 7 days
action: Water and rest advice; sample at end of shift; red or brown urine goes to a doctor
limits: No validation found in hot-climate workers; TCS34725 not validated; vitamins and medicines can change colour; no study links colour to kidney outcomes

esp32_part: QR or RFID check-in at the node
calculation: Check-in to check-out, summed by week
trigger: 55+ hours for 4 weeks in a row
action: Long-term exposure flag; supervisor review; blood pressure check if a clinician agrees
limits: 55 hours comes from WHO/ILO long-term cohort evidence; 4 weeks is unvalidated; this is a health flag, not a legal finding or a disease screen; needs worker safeguards

calculation: 55+ hours and 3+ hot days in a week
limits: No study tests this rule; hours and hot days are both common, so it may fire often; carry-over heat is another hypothesis
